$schema_note: Reference facility-layout data for a Mother Hub / cross-dock sortation center — NOT a storage or fulfillment warehouse. Seeds and validates the layout generator in darkstore-layout-planner.html. Vocabulary (flowPattern, sortationMethod, zone type keys) is aligned 1:1 with ZONE_DEFS / PAINT_DEFS / defaultGenParams() in that file so this can be diffed against generator output directly.

facility_definition.role: Primary regional sorting and consolidation center in a hub-and-spoke parcel network. Receives packed orders from client dark stores/sellers, segregates each shipment into (a) last-mile-hub-bound or (b) other-city-bound, bags/consolidates by destination, and dispatches.
facility_definition.industry_precedent: Term used by Ekart for its primary regional sorting/consolidation tier; equivalent to Delhivery's 'processing centre / sortation facility' tier and generic industry 'parcel sortation center' / 'cross-dock hub'.

dock_door_spacing_ft.note: 12 ft center-to-center is the floor; 14-16 ft reduces MHE congestion at higher door density. Current generator bayW=12 — correct as the safe default, worth exposing 14 ft as a Tier 4-5 option.

dock_door_density.implication: A mother hub needs 3-4x the door density of a storage building of the same footprint — door count should scale with floor area, not just be a flat default.
sources: https://www.steelcobuildings.com/warehouse-loading-dock-design-layout-door-spacing-and-truck-court-planning/ (cross-dock: 1 door per 2,000-3,000 sqft; general distribution center: 1 per 5,000-10,000 sqft; manufacturing: 1 per 15,000-20,000 sqft - corroborates this row's ratio directly)

truck_court_depth_ft.note: Inbound (trunk/linehaul) bays generally need deeper apron than outbound (last-mile van) bays — a ratio the generator does not currently distinguish; both dock bands use the same depth.
sources: https://www.steelcobuildings.com/warehouse-loading-dock-design-layout-door-spacing-and-truck-court-planning/ (130-180ft recommended truck court depth for 53ft trailers - matches this row's full_trailer figure exactly)

aisle_width_ft_by_equipment.note: Matches EQUIPMENT_AISLE_ROWS in server.js and the equipment decision already in the generator — confirmed correct, no change needed.

staging_depth_formula.description: Peak concurrent boxes on the floor = throughput / operating_window_hours * dwell_hours. Already implemented (OP_WINDOW_HOURS / DWELL_HOURS / BOX_SQFT_STAGED in darkstore-layout-planner.html) — confirmed matches how real dwell-driven staging is sized, not a share of daily total volume.

manual.note: Manual sort throughput does not scale by adding headcount past a point — it hits a physical ceiling of walkable pigeonhole/bin faces. Generator's methods table (manual tph:900) is within this real-world range.

semiauto_belt_manual_divert.note: Single linear/modular belt with manual pull-off at destination bins. Generator's semiauto tph:2500 sits mid-range — reasonable.

sortation_throughput_ceiling.generator_note: Generator's automated tph:6000 is conservative relative to real tilt-tray/cross-belt capability (10.8k-25k UPH) — intentionally so, since it's sizing FLOOR FOOTPRINT and staffing needed to feed the sorter, not the sorter's own rated speed. Leave as-is unless the app starts modeling capital equipment cost, where the real ceiling matters.

flow_pattern_rule.i_flow_through_flow: Inbound docks and outbound docks on opposite walls. Mandatory above ~15,000 parcels/day — cross-dock design literature treats I/T-shaped long-narrow buildings as the throughput-scale default specifically to keep arriving and departing vehicle traffic from crossing.
flow_pattern_rule.u_flow_same_wall: Inbound and outbound docks on one wall. Acceptable only at low throughput (Tier 1) or when the building genuinely has doors on one side only — never a first choice at scale.
flow_pattern_rule.generator_status: Correctly implemented: flowPattern i-flow places dockIn at y=0 / dockOut at y=W with real geometric consequence, u-flow keeps both on one wall. No change needed.

destination_lane_placement_principle.name: golden_zone_placement
destination_lane_placement_principle.description: Highest-volume destination lanes should sit closest to the outbound dock / sortation exit to minimize average travel distance; low-volume/long-tail destinations can sit further out or share a lane.
destination_lane_placement_principle.generator_status: NOT currently implemented — outboundLane zones are laid out as evenly-spaced, unweighted slots left-to-right. This is a real gap: a mother hub with a handful of high-volume destinations and many low-volume ones would, in practice, cluster the high-volume lanes nearest the dock. Worth a future decision option (volume-weighted lane order) if per-destination volume ever becomes an input.

labor_flow_principle.one_way_flow: Sortation-to-bagging-to-staging should read as one direction on the plan, no path doubles back through a zone it already passed.
labor_flow_principle.no_cross_traffic: MHE/cart paths for inbound induction and outbound loading should not intersect the same aisle at the same time — this is what the I-flow rule and the lane band sitting strictly between sortation and the outbound dock (not beside it) both protect.
labor_flow_principle.generator_status: Confirmed by the flow ordering in generateDefaultLayout: sort -> stage in lanes -> load is enforced (sort.y < lanes.y < dock.y assertion already tested this session).

dock_door_specifications.description: Added 2026-09-01 from published warehouse-dock design sources, cross-checked against dock_door_spacing_ft/dock_door_density above (they corroborate, not contradict). Physical door object sizing, not layout/spacing rules.

standard_door_size_ft.note: 9ft wide is the industry-preferred width - narrower doors risk trailer/door-track contact and don't allow slightly off-center trailer positioning. Range in practice is 8-10ft wide, 8-10ft tall; 10x12ft for oversized loads, 8x8ft for lighter operations.

dock_platform_height_in.note: Sized to match trailer bed height so a forklift/pallet jack can roll straight across - not a manager-facing layout number in this app today, but relevant if a 3D/elevation view is ever added.

trailer_staging_spaces_per_dock.note: Yard/apron staging spots per active door - genuinely new data point, not previously in this file. Not currently modeled by the generator (truck_court_depth_ft above sizes the apron's DEPTH, not how many trailers queue per door) - worth a future decision option.

dock_door_specifications.app_object_note: This app's own PAINT_DEFS has no distinct 'vehicle dock door' object at this real 9-10ft scale - entry/exit (3x0.5ft) are pedestrian/small-shutter scale, rollshutter (8x1ft) is the closest match to a real dock door's width. Flagged, not changed this pass - the zone-level dockIn/dockOut area budget already accounts for real dock footprint; only the individual door OBJECT is undersized if placed literally.

architectural_symbol_conventions.description: Added 2026-09-01, alongside the drawPaintCell rendering fix it documents (darkstore-layout-planner.html) - real AutoCAD/architectural-drawing door symbol convention, replacing this app's old generic glyph-in-a-box icon for the Door and Fire Exit objects.

components: a straight line breaking the wall (the opening itself)
the door leaf drawn as a straight line, usually shown open
a quarter-circle arc tracing the path the leaf's outer edge travels from closed (flush with the wall) to open
swing_door_symbol.arc_radius_rule: The arc's radius equals the door leaf's own real length - not an arbitrary decorative curve.
swing_door_symbol.generator_status: Implemented in drawPaintCell for PAINT_DEFS.door and PAINT_DEFS.fireexit - leaf + arc, radius = the object's own declared width, oriented by the existing 4-way Rotate control. Entry/Exit (large dock shutters, id 6/7) deliberately kept their own directional-arrow symbol instead - a rolling/coiling shutter doesn't swing on a hinge, so a swing arc would be physically wrong for that object type.

zone_catalog.purpose: Inbound vehicle docking — packed boxes from dark stores/sellers arrive here.
zone_catalog.notes: Fewer, larger vehicles than outbound in most mother-hub feeder patterns (consolidated seller/store pickups) — door count usually LOWER than outbound.

zone_catalog.purpose: Receiving scan / unload buffer directly behind the inbound dock, before boxes enter sortation.
zone_catalog.notes: Only appears when input.inboundStaging is set — should default ON for any mother hub, since receiving scan is universal to the model, not optional.

zone_catalog.purpose: The segregation step: last-mile-hub-bound vs other-city-bound. Conveyor belt with manual or automated divert, OR manual sort stations/pigeonhole wall, depending on sortationMethod.
zone_catalog.notes: This is the zone whose footprint and equipment should scale hardest with sortationMethod — see design_constants.sortation_throughput_ceiling.

zone_catalog.purpose: Sorted shipments packed into destination bags before moving to outbound staging.
zone_catalog.notes: Currently placed as a row of packing+dispatch+table cells above the dock in generateOptimalAiLayout, and as sorting-zone-adjacent PAINT_DEFS.packing in the deep-decisions path — correct concept, could be made its own named zone type for clarity in reporting.

zone_catalog.purpose: Staging lanes grouped BY DESTINATION (one lane per destination city/hub route) — the heart of a cross-dock sort hub.
zone_catalog.notes: Confirmed correctly implemented: one lane per destinationHubs count, width capped by handling equipment, depth sized to peak-wave concurrency. This is the single most load-bearing zone in the whole model — get its sizing right before anything else.

zone_catalog.purpose: Outbound vehicle docking — dispatch to destination hub/city.
zone_catalog.notes: Usually MORE doors than inbound — outbound is destination-fragmented (many smaller vehicles, often one per route) vs inbound's fewer/larger consolidated arrivals. Generator's docks decision (even/outHeavy/inHeavy split) already models this correctly.

zone_catalog.purpose: Missorts, damaged goods, unscannable/unresolved shipments held for manual review.
zone_catalog.notes: Small but universal — every real sort hub has a missort pile. Should probably default ON, currently opt-in.
Only relevant once handlingEquipment moves past manual — could be auto-enabled when equipment != manual instead of a separate opt-in toggle.

zone_catalog.generator_type: security / medical / office / conference / store / ups / bathroom
zone_catalog.purpose: Non-operational support — security desk, first-aid, ops manager office, briefing room, spares store, power room, restrooms.
adjacency: dockIn wall, packed along one side
zone_catalog.notes: Correctly modeled as a packed back-wall band with drop-priority under space pressure.

zone_catalog.purpose: Reserved headroom for volume growth — held-back floor, not built out.

sortation_layout_patterns.description: Fully manual carry: a wall or bank of open-fronted pigeonholes/bins, one per destination, that pickers walk parcels to directly from induction. No conveyor at all.
sortation_layout_patterns.assumed_by: throughput_tiers[tier=1].sortation_description ('Pigeonhole wall or bin-sort by destination, fully manual carry', conveyor_cells_expected: 0)

sortation_layout_patterns.description: A square/rectangular racetrack conveyor loop forms the sortation core; manual sort workers are stationed at fixed positions around its OUTER edge (all 4 sides), picking parcels off the moving belt into destination bins/lanes behind them as it passes — the belt only carries and presents parcels, all sortation decisions and handling stay manual. Distinct from a semiauto divert line (which is usually a single straight/modular spine, not a loop) and from the pigeonhole-wall pattern above (which has no conveyor at all).
sortation_layout_patterns.confirmed_by: reference_layouts[0] below — a real Tier-1-scale facility explicitly labeled 'SORTING AREA (MANUAL SORT)' still uses a conveyor loop, purely to reduce picker walking, not to raise throughput class.
sortation_layout_patterns.correction_to_existing_doc: throughput_tiers[tier=1]'s 'conveyor_cells_expected: 0' is an oversimplification — a manual-sort hub MAY still deploy a low-cost, non-automated loop conveyor. Presence of a conveyor does not by itself imply semiauto/automated sortationMethod; what determines the tier is whether sortation DECISIONS are manual (person reads/decides destination) vs machine-diverted.

reference_layouts.name: Reference Manual-Sort Mother Hub — single-gate split-flow
reference_layouts.source: Real facility floor-plan reference image provided by the user, 2026-09-01 (not generator output, not a fabricated example). Dimensions/areas below are as explicitly labeled on the source drawing.
reference_layouts.how_to_use_this: This is ONE validated real-world instance of the zone_catalog and design_constants above, not a fixed template to reproduce verbatim. Generalize the RATIOS, ADJACENCY, and FLOW PATTERN — the same principles should produce a good layout with these same object types in different positions/proportions for a different building shape or scale, not this exact picture redrawn.

gate.note: ONE shared gate/vehicle apron serves both inbound unload and outbound dispatch — a real-world instance of this app's own gate-flow zone model (ZONE_DEFS.dock = 'Shared Gate'; receiving → sorting → bagging → dispatchQueue sequence) rather than the separate dockIn/dockOut-wall model. Internally, incoming and outbound are still kept on OPPOSITE sides of the building (west vs east) so product never crosses its own path, even with only one exterior gate — a hybrid of design_constants.flow_pattern_rule's u_flow (one gate) and i_flow (opposite-side separation) reasoning, not a pure case of either.

support_band.vs_doc_range: Below zone_catalog's support_rooms typical_share_of_footprint_pct (8-14%) — plausibly because absolute admin/utility footprint doesn't scale down linearly with a smaller Tier-1 building. Noted, not silently forced to match.

zones.label: Staff Room
zones.note: Closest existing ZONE_DEFS match for a break/staff room — not an exact concept match, kept for consistency with the app's current zone vocabulary rather than inventing a new type for one reference.

zones.label: Storage Area
zones.note: Auxiliary shelving/spares storage, not core sortation-lane storage — sits in the support band, not the operational flow.

operational_zones.label: Sorting Area (Manual Sort)
operational_zones.note: Square core, perimeter conveyor loop, manual sort stations on all 4 outer sides — see sortation_layout_patterns.manual_perimeter_loop.

reference_layouts.flow_pattern: gate (south, shared) -> splits internally to receiving (west band) and dispatchQueue (east band) -> both feed/drain the central sorting loop -> sorted parcels move to outboundLane staging (lane-wise by destination, east-center) -> dispatchQueue -> gate. One-way, no crossed paths, despite only one physical gate.

area_accounting.note: Roughly two-thirds of this real reference's interior is open floor — the walkway ring around the sorting loop, handling space between zones, and the gate's interior apron — none of it separately named. Real Tier-1 manual hubs run leaner on named/walled area and heavier on open interior floor than a naive reading of zone_catalog's individual percentages (which sum toward a denser-looking budget) would suggest; open circulation is not wasted space here, it's load-bearing for manual handling.

throughput_tiers.name: Micro Manual Hub
throughput_tiers.sortation_description: Pigeonhole wall or bin-sort by destination, fully manual carry from induction to bag.
throughput_tiers.notes: U-flow acceptable at this scale — low door count means arriving/departing traffic rarely actually conflicts. Generator's existing i-flow default is still fine here; u-flow is a valid alternative, not a requirement.

throughput_tiers.name: Small Conveyor-Assisted Hub
throughput_tiers.sortation_description: Single straight conveyor spine from induction to a manual-divert sort line — workers pull parcels off the belt into destination bins as it passes.
throughput_tiers.conveyor_cells_expected: spine 1 cell wide, full span between support-room band and sortation zone
throughput_tiers.notes: This is the tier where I-flow becomes non-negotiable — door count is high enough that same-wall traffic would genuinely conflict.

throughput_tiers.name: Medium Hybrid Hub
throughput_tiers.sortation_description: Modular/roller belt with scan-and-divert chutes at destination points — semi-automated, still some manual handling at induction and exception.
throughput_tiers.conveyor_cells_expected: wider spine (2 cells) or short loop, matches automated-tier footprint but on a modular-belt (5000 UPH class) throughput budget
throughput_tiers.notes: Sits at the manual/automated boundary — generator's binary semiauto/automated choice is a reasonable simplification of what's really a continuum.

throughput_tiers.name: Large Automated Mother Hub

dock_doors.note: Approaches the 1-per-2500-3000-sqft cross-dock density benchmark at the top of this range.

throughput_tiers.sortation_description: Tilt-tray or cross-belt automated sorter, dozens to 100+ destination chutes feeding directly into bagging/lane groups.
throughput_tiers.conveyor_cells_expected: double-wide spine, generator's automated method already draws this
throughput_tiers.notes: Consider 14 ft door spacing over the 12 ft default at this scale — door-adjacent MHE congestion becomes a real constraint above ~40 doors on one wall.

throughput_tiers.name: Mega Regional Mother Hub
throughput_tiers.sortation_description: Multiple parallel cross-belt/tilt-tray sorter loops feeding a large destination-lane bank; often a T- or multi-wing plan with several inbound clusters converging on one central sortation core.
throughput_tiers.conveyor_cells_expected: multiple parallel spines, likely beyond what a single generateDefaultLayout pass models today
throughput_tiers.notes: At this scale a single-block I-flow band model (current generator's whole geometry) starts to understate real layouts, which usually break into wings or multiple sortation cores. Flagged as a known ceiling on the current generator's applicability, not a bug — most mother hubs the app will actually be used for sit in Tiers 1-4.

already_correct: I-flow vs U-flow real geometric consequence (dockIn/dockOut wall placement)
Dock door spacing constant (bayW=12ft) matches industry minimum
Equipment-driven aisle width (EQUIPMENT_AISLE_ROWS) matches real MHE clearance standards
Peak-concurrent staging depth formula (throughput x dwell / operating window, not daily total)
Outbound-heavier door split available and correctly reasoned against destination count
One-way sort -> stage -> load flow ordering enforced in geometry
gaps_found_this_pass: sortationMethod had zero geometric effect until this session's fix — now draws 0/1-wide/2-wide conveyor spine for manual/semiauto/automated
Photo-upload path used to bypass the generator entirely and paint raw AI-guessed geometry — now routed through the same deterministic pipeline as manual entry
gaps_still_open: No door-count scaling by floor area (cross-dock density benchmark: 1 door per 2500-3000 sqft) — door count today comes purely from the doors decision's frontage cap, not footprint
No inbound-vs-outbound truck-court depth distinction (linehaul trucks need deeper apron than last-mile vans)
No volume-weighted destination-lane placement (golden-zone principle) — lanes are evenly spaced regardless of per-destination volume
inboundStage and exception zones are opt-in when they're near-universal in a real mother hub — worth defaulting ON
14 ft door spacing option not exposed for Tier 4-5 scale
